records.statement: One categorical variable can be summarized with counts/proportions, while quantitative variables require numerical summaries and inspection of distribution shape.
For a symmetric quantitative distribution the mean is often preferred; for skewed distributions or distributions with outliers, the median is often preferred because it is more resistant to outliers.

Standard deviation is a common variability measure for interval- or ratio-level variables; the five-number summary and interquartile range are also available descriptive summaries for quantitative data.

records.statement: The pooled two-sample t procedure for comparing two population means requires independent random samples from normal populations with equal variances; the source describes independence as the most critical condition.
records.section: Chapter 6.2 Inferences about two population central values: independent samples

records.statement: When population variances differ, the text presents a separate-variance t procedure and notes it is more reliable than a pooled t procedure when sample sizes and variances are very unequal.
Paired samples are dependent observations matched in a meaningful way, commonly repeated measurements on the same participant; inference is conducted on within-pair difference scores.
Penn State states that a paired-means t procedure requires paired data and a normally distributed population of differences, or a sample size of at least 30 for the course's approximation rule.
Using multiple independent t tests to compare more than two group means increases the chance of Type I error; one-way ANOVA provides an overall multi-group comparison.
